{{Short description|Australian basketball player (born 2004)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2025}}{{Use Australian English|date=February 2024}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Johnny Furphy | image = Johnny Furphy Paris NBA Game 20250123 (cropped).jpg | image_size = 155px | caption = Furphy with the [[Indiana Pacers]] in 2025 | position = [[Shooting guard]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 8 | weight_lbs = 200 | league = [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] | team = Indiana Pacers | number = 12 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2004|12|8|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Melbourne|Melbourne, Victoria]], Australia | high_school = [[Maribyrnong College]]
(Melbourne, Victoria) | college = [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] (2023–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 35 | draft_team = [[San Antonio Spurs]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = 2021 | team1 = Hawthorn Magic | years2 = 2022–2023 | team2 = [[BA Centre of Excellence]] | years3 = {{nbay|2024|start}}–present | team3 = [[Indiana Pacers]] | years4 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team4 = →[[Indiana Mad Ants]] | highlights = * [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Freshman team (2024) }} '''John William Furphy''' (born 8 December 2004) is an Australian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]], where he earned All-[[Big 12 Conference men's basketball|Big 12]] Freshman Team honors. Furphy was selected 35th overall by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the second round of the [[2024 NBA draft]] and was subsequently traded to the Pacers. He made his NBA debut during the [[2024–25 NBA season]] and appeared in the [[2025 NBA Finals]]. == Early life == Furphy was born on 8 December 2004 in [[Melbourne|Melbourne, Victoria]], and grew up in the [[Suburbs and localities (Australia)|suburb]] of [[Clifton Hill, Victoria|Clifton Hill]].{{Cite web |title=Johnny Furphy {{!}} Guard {{!}} Indiana Pacers |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1642277/johnny-furphy/bio |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122224644/https://www.nba.com/player/1642277/johnny-furphy/bio |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=18 October 2025 |website=[[NBA]]}}{{Cite web |last=Rolfe |first=Peter |date=23 June 2024 |title=‘It’s super crazy to think I will be up on that stage. It will be a dream come true.’ |url=https://www.heraldsun.com.au/news/victoria/its-super-crazy-to-think-i-will-be-up-on-that-stage-it-will-be-a-dream-come-true/news-story/aab8a440f4035399af2a693a8c74c889 |url-access=subscription |access-date=18 October 2025 |website=[[Herald Sun]]}} From an early age, he aspired to earn a [[Athletic scholarship|college scholarship]] in the [[United States]], a goal he expressed while in fifth grade.{{Cite web |last=Pierik |first=Jon |date=25 June 2024 |title=Here’s Johnny! How a kid from Clifton Hill rose to the NBA draft |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/here-s-johnny-how-a-kid-from-clifton-hill-rose-to-the-nba-draft-20240625-p5jog8.html |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122194200/https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/here-s-johnny-how-a-kid-from-clifton-hill-rose-to-the-nba-draft-20240625-p5jog8.html |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=21 November 2025 |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]}} He attended [[Maribyrnong College]], where he was a member of the [[Maribyrnong College#Specialist Sport Program|Maribyrnong Sports Academy]], an elite sports program at the school. Furphy enrolled as a basketball athlete and Year 7 student in 2017 and graduated in 2022.{{cite web |date=22 June 2024 |title=MSA Alumnus Johnny Furphy invited to Green Room for NBA draft |url=https://sportsacademy.maribsc.vic.edu.au/news-and-media/2024/6/22/msa-alumnus-johnny-furphy-invited-to-green-room-for-nba-draft |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122071329/https://sportsacademy.maribsc.vic.edu.au/news-and-media/2024/6/22/msa-alumnus-johnny-furphy-invited-to-green-room-for-nba-draft |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=24 June 2024 |work=[[Maribyrnong College]]}} During high school, he was a multi-sport athlete, competing in [[basketball]], [[cricket]], and [[Australian rules football|football]]. He stated that football served as his secondary option if his basketball career did not materialize. == Semi-professional career == During his teenage years, Furphy competed in various semi-professional [[Basketball in Australia#League system|basketball leagues across Australia]].{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Matthew |date=17 June 2025 |title=Who Is Johnny Furphy? What to Know About Indiana Pacers' 20-Year-Old Fan Favorite |url=https://www.nbc.com/nbc-insider/who-is-johnny-furphy-what-to-know-about-indiana-pacers-rookie |access-date=21 November 2025 |website=[[NBC]]}} He played in the [[Big V]] for two seasons from 2021 to 2022. During the 2021 season, he played for the Hawthorn Magic in the Championship division, appearing in just two games before the season was cancelled midway due to the [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on basketball|COVID-19 pandemic]]. That season, he averaged 2.0 points and 1.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Johnny Furphy |url=https://www.basketballvictoria.com.au/bigv/player/ef02940e-76a3-11eb-bf75-6ec8402b0194/2a41187a-aa42-11eb-b7b2-769414a21556/johnny-furphy |access-date=27 June 2024 |work=[[Big V]]}} The following year, he started the 2022 season playing for the [[University of Melbourne#Sports and athletics|Melbourne University Black Angels]] in the Division One, appearing in nine games and averaging 12.6 points and 4.0 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Johnny Furphy |url=https://www.basketballvictoria.com.au/bigv/player/83a5f656-8435-11ec-8128-b55682bb0e92/2a41187a-aa42-11eb-b7b2-769414a21556/johnny-furphy |access-date=28 June 2024 |work=[[Big V]]}} Midway through that season, Furphy relocated to [[Canberra]] to join the [[BA Centre of Excellence|Basketball Australia Centre of Excellence]] (CoE), competing in the [[NBL1]] for two seasons from 2022 to 2023.{{Cite web |last=Newton |first=Phina |date=11 October 2024 |title=From the Melbourne University Basketball Club to the NBA |url=https://sport.unimelb.edu.au/news/from-melbourne-university-basketball-club-to-the-nba |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250319142553/https://sport.unimelb.edu.au/news/from-melbourne-university-basketball-club-to-the-nba |archive-date=19 March 2025 |access-date=21 November 2025 |website=[[University of Melbourne#Sports and athletics|Melbourne University Sport]]}} Furphy appeared in three games for the CoE in July of the [[2022 NBL1 season|2022 season]] and remained with the team for the [[2023 NBL1 season|2023 season]], during which he averaged 14.3 points and 5.6 rebounds per game over 12 games.{{cite web |title=Johnny Furphy |url=https://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Johnny-Furphy/605390 |url-access=subscription |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240516123956/https://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Johnny-Furphy/605390 |archive-date=16 May 2024 |access-date=27 June 2024 |website=US Basket}}{{cite web Athletic]]}} ==College career== Furphy committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] in the [[United States]] after signing his [[National Letter of Intent|national letter of intent]] on 3 August 2023. He chose Kansas over offers from [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{Cite web |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=11 August 2023 |title=New KU basketball small forward Johnny Furphy working out with NBL team in Australia |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article278152827.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122200518/https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article278152827.html |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=[[Kansas City Star]]}} Days after his commitment, Furphy participated in a training session that included [[Exhibition game|scrimmages]] and basketball drills with the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). Later that month, he relocated to [[Lawrence, Kansas]], to begin his college career at the [[University of Kansas]].{{Cite web |last=Pereira |first=Aaron |date=8 August 2023 |title=Aussie Basketball Wunderkind Trains with Phoenix |url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/aussie-basketball-wunderkind-trains-with-phoenix |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122073932/https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/aussie-basketball-wunderkind-trains-with-phoenix |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=[[South East Melbourne Phoenix]]}}{{Cite web |date=7 August 2023 |title=Johnny Furphy Interview (August 8, 2023) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIA9kBsJAZ0 |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=[[YouTube]] |publisher=[[South East Melbourne Phoenix]]}} Furphy made his collegiate debut as a [[Redshirt (college sports)#Terminology|true freshman]] in the season opener against [[2023–24 North Carolina Central Eagles men's basketball team|North Carolina Central]] on 6 November 2023, recording six points and five rebounds in a 99–56 victory.{{Cite web |last=Laddha |first=Shreyas |date=6 November 2023 |title=KU basketball dominates North Carolina Central in season opener. Here are 3 takeaways |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article281489408.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122201024/https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article281489408.html |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=21 November 2025 |website=[[Kansas City Star]]}} He made his first career [[Starting lineup|start]] against [[Chaminade Silverswords|Chaminade]] on 20 November, contributing four points and two rebounds in an 83–56 win.{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Kyle |date=20 November 2023 |title=Hawking Points: Kanas Takes Care of Chaminade in Maui Invitational Opener |url=https://www.si.com/college/kansas/basketball/hawking-points-kanas-takes-care-of-chaminade-in-maui-invitational-opener |access-date=21 November 2025 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} Furphy delivered his best collegiate performance against [[2023–24 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]] on 22 January 2024, posting season highs of 23 points and 11 rebounds in a 74–69 victory.{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Kyle |date=29 May 2024 |title=Johnny Furphy to Remain in NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/college/kansas/basketball/johnny-furphy-to-remain-in-nba-draft-01hz3ehrzac3 |access-date=21 November 2025 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} He played his final college game during the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Midwest regional – Detroit, Michigan|Round of 32]] in the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2024 NCAA tournament]], tallying nine points and seven rebounds in an 89–68 loss to [[2023–24 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]] on 23 March.{{Cite web |last=Laddha |first=Shreyas |date=24 March 2024 |title=Who’s staying and going from the 2023-24 Kansas Jayhawks basketball roster? |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article287038070.html November 2025 |website=[[Kansas City Star]]}} Kansas finished their [[2023–24 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|season]] with a 23–11 record, during which Furphy played a significant role as a reserve [[Swingman#Basketball|wing]].{{cite web |last=Swain |first=Michael |date=4 December 2023 |title=Johnny Furphy embracing his role off the bench for KU basketball |url=https://247sports.com/college/kansas/article/johnny-furphy-kansas-basketball-role-222344580/ |access-date=20 February 2024 |website=[[247Sports]]}} He played in 33 games with 19 starts, averaging 9.0 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 1.0 assists per game while shooting 46.6 percent from the field.{{cite web |title=Johnny Furphy 2023-24 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/johnny-furphy-1/gamelog/2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250210171324/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/johnny-furphy-1/gamelog/2024 |archive-date=10 February 2025 |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}} Furphy’s standout rookie performance earned him selection to the [[2023–24 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12]] All-Freshman Team.{{Cite web |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=16 April 2024 |title=Kansas basketball freshman Johnny Furphy declares for the 2024 NBA Draft |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article287748580.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122212719/https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article287748580.html |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=[[Kansas City Star]]}} After the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]], Furphy declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] on 16 April 2024, forgoing his remaining [[National Collegiate Athletic Association#Player eligibility|college eligibility]]. He later received an invitation to the draft [[2024 NBA draft#Invited attendees|green room]], having been projected to be an early-round draft pick.{{Cite web |last=Salerno |first=Cameron |date=19 June 2024 |title=2024 NBA Draft: UConn's Donovan Clingan, French prospects among 24 players to accept green room invites |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2024-nba-draft-uconns-donovan-clingan-french-prospects-among-24-players-to-accept-green-room-invites/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250714194739/https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2024-nba-draft-uconns-donovan-clingan-french-prospects-among-24-players-to-accept-green-room-invites/ |archive-date=14 July 2025 |access-date=21 November 2025 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}} Having grown up as an [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] fan, particularly admiring [[LeBron James]] and rooting for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], Furphy expressed excitement about fulfilling his long-held childhood dream of competing on the same court as his basketball idols. ==Professional career== ===Indiana Pacers (2024–present)=== ====2024–25==== Furphy was selected 35th overall by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the second round of the [[2024 NBA draft]] on 27 June 2024. Later that same night, he was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for the 36th overall pick, [[Juan Núñez (basketball)|Juan Núñez]], and cash considerations.{{Cite web |last=East |first=Tony |date=27 June 2024 |title=Indiana Pacers take Johnny Furphy at pick 35 after a draft night trade with San Antonio Spurs |url=https://www.si.com/nba/pacers/onsi/roster/indiana-pacers-take-johnny-furphy-at-pick-35-after-a-draft-night-trade-with-san-antonio-spurs |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} He signed a four-year contract worth $8.59 million with the Pacers on 6 July.{{Cite web |title=Johnny Furphy {{!}} NBA Contracts & Salaries |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nba/player/_/id/91768 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122213344/https://www.spotrac.com/nba/player/_/id/91768 |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=Spotrac.com}}{{Cite web |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=7 July 2024 |title=Former KU wing Johnny Furphy signs NBA rookie contract with Indiana Pacers |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article289835784.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122213343/https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article289835784.html |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=[[Kansas City Star]]}} Furphy made his [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) debut on 25 October 2024, at the age of 19 in a game against the [[2024–25 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]]. He entered the game late in the fourth quarter with 4:59 remaining, while the Pacers were trailing 113–83. Furphy did not score in the game, missing all three of his field goal attempts and one three-point attempt. The Pacers ultimately lost the game 123–98.{{Cite web |title=Indiana Pacers at New York Knicks Box Score, October 25, 2024 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410250NYK.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122221236/https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410250NYK.html |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=21 November 2025 |website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}}{{Cite web |title=Johnny Furphy 2024-25 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/f/furphjo01/gamelog/2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122221109/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/f/furphjo01/gamelog/2025 |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}} Months after his initial debut, Furphy delivered his best NBA performance against the [[2024–25 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]] on 11 April 2025, in what was the second-last game of the Pacers' regular season. In a 129–115 loss, he scored a career-high 17 points with six rebounds and three assists in a then-career-high 32 minutes played.{{Cite web |last=Hotchkiss |first=Wheat |date=11 April 2025 |title=Game Rewind: Pacers 115, Magic 129 |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/rewind-pacers-magic-250411 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250622055251/https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/rewind-pacers-magic-250411 |archive-date=22 June 2025 |access-date=12 April 2025 |website=[[Indiana Pacers]]}} Furphy finished the [[2024–25 Indiana Pacers season|2024–25 NBA season]] having played in 50 games, all substitutions coming off the bench, averaging 2.1 points, 1.4 rebounds, and 0.4 assists per game while shooting 38.0 percent from the field.{{Cite web |title=Johnny Furphy Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/f/furphjo01.html |access-date=3 December 2025 |website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}} As a [[rookie]], Furphy primarily served as a [[Substitution (sport)|substitute]] to [[Resting the starters|rest starters]] and gain playing time in the closing minutes of games with decided outcomes. Throughout the season, he was frequently [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] to the [[Noblesville Boom|Indiana Mad Ants]],{{cite web |title=2024-2025 Indiana Mad Ants Transaction History |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Indiana-Mad-Ants/68/Transaction_History/2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250622055251/https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Indiana-Mad-Ants/68/Transaction_History/2025 |archive-date=22 June 2025 |access-date=17 January 2025 |website=[[RealGM]]}} the Pacers' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, shuttling between the Mad Ants and the Pacers' bench. Furphy made his G League debut on 7 January 2025 in a game against the [[Maine Celtics]], recording 11 points, eight rebounds, and one assist in a 118–115 victory.{{Cite web |date=7 January 2025 |title=Mad Ants Prevail Over Celtics Behind Freeman’s Career Day |url=https://noblesville.gleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-prevail-over-celtics-behind-freemans-career-day |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112184045/https://noblesville.gleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-prevail-over-celtics-behind-freemans-career-day |archive-date=12 January 2026 |access-date=30 November 2025 |website=[[Noblesville Boom]]}}{{Cite web |date=7 January 2025 |title=MNE vs IMA |url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2022400069/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112182923/https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2022400069/ |archive-date=12 January 2026 |access-date=12 January 2026 |website=NBA G League Stats |publisher=NBA Media Ventures}} He finished the [[2024–25 NBA G League season]] having started 10 games, averaging 14.3 points, 9.6 rebounds, and 1.8 assists per game while shooting 45.3 percent from the field.{{Cite web |title=Johnny Furphy |url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/player/1642277/career/ |url-status=live |publisher=NBA Media Ventures}} ====2025–26==== Furphy began the [[2025–26 Indiana Pacers season|2025–26 NBA season]] with limited playing time due to injuries affecting his left foot and ankle that started during the [[2025–26 Indiana Pacers season#Preseason|preseason]].{{Cite web |last=Dopirak |first=Dustin |date=3 November 2025 |title=Pacers forward Johnny Furphy leaves game vs Bucks with another left foot injury |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2025/11/03/johnny-furphy-injury-update-pacers-forward-leaves-game-due-to-ankle/87076719007/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122222816/https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2025/11/03/johnny-furphy-injury-update-pacers-forward-leaves-game-due-to-ankle/87076719007/ |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=[[IndyStar]]}}{{cite web |title=Johnny Furphy 2025-26 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/f/furphjo01/gamelog/2026/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122222047/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/f/furphjo01/gamelog/2026/ |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=21 November 2025 |website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}} During a game against the [[2025–26 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]] on 3 November 2025, he sustained a [[Sprained ankle|sprain]] to his left ankle after falling while driving to the basket in the fourth quarter. Following the game, which ended in a 117–115 loss, Furphy was seen leaving the locker room using [[Crutch|crutches]].{{Cite web |date=3 November 2025 |title=Pacers' Johnny Furphy: Doesn't return vs. Milwaukee |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-johnny-furphy-doesnt-return-vs-milwaukee/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122084836/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-johnny-furphy-doesnt-return-vs-milwaukee/ |archive-date=22 November 2025 |access-date=21 November 2025 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}} He returned to action on 3 December after missing 14 games.{{cite web |title=Johnny Furphy 2025-26 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/f/furphjo01/gamelog/2026/ |website=basketball-reference.com |access-date=10 February 2026}} On 8 February 2026, he sustained a [[anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn right ACL]] in the Pacers' 122–104 loss to the [[2025–26 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]], which saw him be ruled out for the rest of the season.{{cite news |title=Confirmed ACL tear for Aussie NBA gun Johnny Furphy |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/47881298/nba-aussie-johnny-furphy-acl-tear-confirmed-indiana-pacers |access-date=10 February 2026 |work=ESPN.com |date=9 February 2026 |language=en}} He made 34 appearances and 21 starts in his second season with Indiana, averaging 5.2 points, 4.4 rebounds, 1.1 assists, and 18.5 minutes of court time per game. == Player profile == Furphy is 6 feet 8 inches (2.03 m) tall and weighs 200 pounds (91 kg).
